lines.en: Good morning! That oak table is one of my best pieces, and I am asking three hundred dollars for it.
lines.pt: Bom dia! Aquela mesa de carvalho é uma das minhas melhores peças, e estou pedindo trezentos dólares por ela.

lines.en: It is beautiful, but my budget is two hundred dollars. What if we met halfway on the price?
lines.pt: Ela é linda, mas meu orçamento é de duzentos dólares. E se a gente se encontrasse no meio do caminho no preço?

lines.en: Halfway would be two hundred and fifty. I spent weeks fixing it, so the work is not cheap.
lines.pt: O meio-termo seriam duzentos e cinquenta. Passei semanas consertando a mesa, então o trabalho não é barato.

lines.en: I understand that. Would you consider two hundred and sixty if I pick it up myself today?
lines.pt: Entendo. Você consideraria duzentos e sessenta se eu mesmo buscasse hoje?

lines.en: Delivery usually costs me money, so that helps. In that case, I could go down to two eighty.
lines.pt: A entrega costuma me custar dinheiro, então isso ajuda. Nesse caso, eu poderia baixar para duzentos e oitenta.

lines.en: That is closer. What if I took those two chairs as well, if you gave me a discount on both?
lines.pt: Está mais perto. E se eu levasse aquelas duas cadeiras também, se você me desse um desconto nas duas?

lines.en: The chairs are old, though. They need some repair, and I was not planning to sell them separately.
lines.pt: As cadeiras são velhas, porém. Precisam de reparo, e eu não pretendia vendê-las separadas.

lines.en: Fair enough. Still, there is a small scratch on one leg of the table, so two seventy seems reasonable.
lines.pt: Justo. Mesmo assim, há um pequeno arranhão numa perna da mesa, então duzentos e setenta parece razoável.

lines.en: You noticed the scratch! Okay, in that case I will accept two seventy-five, and I will wrap it for you.
lines.pt: Você notou o arranhão! Certo, nesse caso aceito duzentos e setenta e cinco, e embrulho para você.

lines.en: Deal. I am glad we reached a compromise, and honestly this table is a bargain. Do you take cards?
lines.pt: Fechado. Fico feliz que chegamos a um acordo, e sinceramente essa mesa é uma pechincha. Você aceita cartão?

lines.en: Of course. Thanks for being so reasonable; most customers just walk away when I will not move on the price.
lines.pt: Claro. Obrigado por ser tão razoável; a maioria dos clientes vai embora quando eu não cedo no preço.

facts.big: what if · would you consider · in that case
facts.label: Negociar um preço
facts.sub: Proponha com What if we met halfway? Peça com Would you consider…? Feche com In that case, I will…

facts.label: Propor uma ideia
facts.sub: What if + passado simples sugere uma possibilidade de forma suave: What if we met halfway on the price? What if I picked it up today?

facts.label: Pedir abertura
facts.sub: Would you consider + substantivo ou -ing é um pedido muito educado: Would you consider two sixty? Would you consider lowering the price?

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: What if we met halfway? is a polite way to suggest a compromise.
items.why: It invites the seller to move too.

items.s: Would you consider…? is rude in a negotiation.
items.why: It is a soft, polite request.

items.s: In that case means because of what you just said.
items.why: It links to the new condition.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: What if we met halfway? is a polite way to suggest a compromise. → Verdadeiro (It invites the seller to move too.)
Would you consider…? is rude in a negotiation. → Falso (It is a soft, polite request.)
In that case means because of what you just said. → Verdadeiro (It links to the new condition.)

pages.title: A table at the market · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Saturday at a busy market in Portland. People walk between the stalls with coffee. Dan stops at a table full of old furniture. Blake, the seller, smiles and waits. Many things here look overpriced to Dan. He loves to haggle, but politely.

“Good morning! That oak table is one of my best pieces, and I am asking three hundred dollars for it.” says Blake. “It is beautiful, but my budget is two hundred dollars. What if we met halfway on the price?” says Dan. “Halfway would be two hundred and fifty. I spent weeks fixing it, so the work is not cheap.” says Blake.
